title: Bouncing ball

caveats: slight motion blur and elongation during fast fall

reference.basis: banded black-and-white stick taken as 1.0 m metre stick with ~10 segments in a room-scale scene

slow_motion.evidence: No narration, captions or on-screen text indicate slow motion; assume real time.

subjects.description: small glossy green spherical ball that drops and bounces

observation.what_happens: A small green ball drops from just below a black-and-white striped bar at the top and falls to the brown floor. It bounces several times while drifting rightward, then rolls along the floor to the right.

calibration.note: striped scale bar = 1 m (banded black-and-white stick taken as 1.0 m metre stick with ~10 segments in a room-scale scene) spans 531 px in SAM's mask

given: scale: striped scale bar = 1 m (banded black-and-white stick taken as 1.0 m metre stick with ~10 segments in a room-scale scene) spans 531 px in SAM's mask, known to ±30%
reasoning: x drifts right almost steadily while y shows repeated parabolic arcs with decreasing peak height, classic gravity flight with floor impacts losing energy. Restitution ~0.7 explains the peak ratio and floor sits near y~-0.87 m. Candidates go from vacuum ballistic bounce to linear Stokes drag to quadratic turbulent drag with bounce friction to test if air matters.

law.title: Clean bounce, no air
law.summary: The ball flies in parabolas under gravity and loses bounce height only at the floor hit.

params.name: e
params.meaning: normal restitution, rebound over impact speed

fitted.title: Clean bounce, no air
fitted.summary: The ball flies in parabolas under gravity and loses bounce height only at the floor hit.

params.name: e
params.meaning: normal restitution, rebound over impact speed

candidates.ifItWins: Flight is vacuum-ballistic and all energy loss is in a single normal restitution; air drag and floor friction are negligible.

law.title: Bouncy ball with light air drag
law.summary: Like the simple bounce but air gently drags the ball and each bounce also rubs a little forward speed away.

params.name: f
params.meaning: tangential retention of vx at bounce

fitted.title: Bouncy ball with light air drag
fitted.summary: Like the simple bounce but air gently drags the ball and each bounce also rubs a little forward speed away.

params.name: f
params.meaning: tangential retention of vx at bounce

candidates.ifItWins: Air slows the ball smoothly in flight and the floor also scrubs forward speed, so both air viscosity and floor friction matter.

law.title: Bouncy ball with fast-air drag
law.summary: Like the simple bounce but air resistance pushes much harder when the ball moves fast.

params.name: f
params.meaning: tangential retention of vx at bounce

fitted.title: Bouncy ball with fast-air drag
fitted.summary: Like the simple bounce but air resistance pushes much harder when the ball moves fast.

params.name: f
params.meaning: tangential retention of vx at bounce

candidates.ifItWins: Fast flight drag grows as speed squared, pointing to turbulent air drag on the ball rather than slow viscous drag.

law.title: Textbook projectile (no air)
law.summary: Moves at constant horizontal speed while gravity pulls it down at a constant rate.

fitted.title: Textbook projectile (no air)
fitted.summary: Moves at constant horizontal speed while gravity pulls it down at a constant rate.

caveats: Scale bar is uncertain by about a third so absolute gravity and floor height stay loose
Rolling phase after bounces is treated as simple sliding with no spin
All bounces are assumed to share the same bounciness
critique.finding: The ball falls under gravity {g} and hits the floor at {y_floor}. Each bounce springs back upward keeping {e} of its falling speed.
critique.headline: The ball bounces cleanly with almost no air drag.
critique.why_it_won: It includes the floor bounces that the no-bounce textbook flight misses, without adding air drag that the data do not need.

headline: The ball bounces cleanly with almost no air drag.
finding: The ball falls under gravity 9.8 ± 2.9 m/s² and hits the floor at -0.87 ± 0.26 m. Each bounce springs back upward keeping 0.700032 ± 0.000088 of its falling speed.

eyeball.confidence: medium: free-fall time and bounce height estimated visually against 1m bar, within ~30% scale uncertainty
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical motion is constant acceleration free fall y = y0 + vy0*t + 0.5*g*t^2, with ground contact at y_floor and normal rebound vy_after = -e*vy_before
